triples.relationship: same-book prohibition concerning a neighbor's wrong within the heart
triples.rationale: Both instructions prohibit retaining or reckoning another person's wrong within one's heart. Chapter 7 names a brother and chapter 8 a neighbor; the repeated inward ethical demand accompanies wider commands for just communal conduct.
triples.source_text: Do not reckon your neighbor’s wrong in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, for I hate all these things, says the Lord Almighty.”

target_units.text: Do not oppress widow, orphan, newcomer or poor person, and let no one harbor resentment for his brother’s wrong in your hearts.”

triples.relationship: mourning transformed into gladness
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises that Judah's appointed fasts will become joy and good festivals. The psalm's speaker likewise thanks the Lord for turning lament into dancing and replacing sackcloth with gladness. Both explicitly reverse mourning into joy, while one concerns communal observances and the other personal deliverance.
triples.source_text: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: The fourth fast, the fifth fast, the seventh fast and the tenth fast will become joy, gladness and good festivals for Judah’s house. You will rejoice; love truth and peace.

target_units.text: The Lord heard and had mercy on me; the Lord became my helper.
Thou didst turn my lament into dancing for me; Thou didst tear open my sackcloth and gird me with gladness,

triples.relationship: many peoples drawn toward the Lord's Jerusalem
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces the coming of many peoples and city residents, explained in the following units as seeking the Lord in Jerusalem. Isaiah likewise promises nations coming to the Lord's mountain and house, with His word proceeding from Jerusalem. Both picture a broad gathering toward that center.
triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Many peoples and residents of many cities will yet come.

target_units.text: In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,

and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

triples.relationship: peoples invite one another to seek the Lord
triples.rationale: Zechariah's city residents urge one another to go entreat and seek the Lord. Isaiah likewise reports many nations saying to one another, 'Come, let us go up' to His mountain and house. Both present the gathering through the visitors' shared invitation.
triples.source_text: Residents of five cities will come together into one city, saying, ‘Let us go to entreat the Lord’s presence and seek the presence of the Lord Almighty. I too will go.’

target_units.text: and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

triples.relationship: many nations coming to the Lord's mountain and house
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises many peoples and nations seeking the Lord Almighty in Jerusalem. Micah likewise describes peoples hurrying to the Lord's mountain and many nations coming to His house, with His word going out from Jerusalem. The destination and multinational gathering closely correspond.
triples.source_text: Many peoples and many nations will come to seek the presence of the Lord Almighty in Jerusalem and appease the Lord’s presence.

target_units.text: In the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, established upon the mountain summits and raised above the hills, and peoples will hurry toward it.

Many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. They will show us His way, and we will walk in His paths.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

triples.relationship: outsiders seek association because God is among His people
triples.rationale: Zechariah's people from many languages grasp a Jewish man's garment and ask to accompany him because they heard God is with his people. Isaiah likewise depicts outsiders following and acknowledging that God is in the addressed community. The connection concerns recognized divine presence; Isaiah's bondage imagery is not transferred to Zechariah's request.
triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord Almighty: In those days, when ten men from all the nations’ languages take hold and grasp the fringe of a Jewish man’s garment, saying, ‘We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you all.’”

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord Sabaoth: “Egypt toiled, and the Ethiopians’ trade; and the Seboin, tall men, will cross over to you and become your slaves. They will follow behind you, bound with handcuffs, bow to you, and pray in you, because God is in you. They will say, ‘There is no God besides Thee;

triples.relationship: the Lord's gaze upon human beings
triples.rationale: Zechariah says that the Lord watches human beings and all Israel's tribes within an oracle naming surrounding lands. The psalm likewise says He sees all humanity and looks upon all earth's inhabitants. Both expressly extend His gaze across human life.
triples.source_text: An oracle of the Lord’s word: in Sedrach’s land and Damascus is His sacrifice, because the Lord watches human beings and all Israel’s tribes,

target_units.text: From heaven the Lord looked down; He saw all the sons of men.
From His prepared dwelling place He looked upon all who inhabit the earth.
He formed their hearts individually; He understands all their deeds.

triples.relationship: Tyre's wisdom and understanding within a judgment oracle
triples.rationale: Zechariah includes Tyre and Sidon in the oracle and describes them as exceedingly wise. Ezekiel addresses Tyre's ruler and examines his claimed wisdom, understanding, wealth and resulting pride. Both place Tyre's wisdom within prophetic scrutiny, without transferring Sidon or the ruler's precise claims between them.
triples.source_text: and Emath within its borders, Tyre and Sidon, because they were exceedingly wise.

target_units.text: “And you, son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre: Thus says the Lord: Because your heart was exalted and you said, ‘I am a god; I have inhabited a god’s dwelling in the heart of the sea’—yet you are a human, and not a god, and you made your heart like a god’s heart—
Surely you are not wiser than Daniel? Did wise men not instruct you in their knowledge?
Surely it was not by your knowledge or understanding that you built up strength for yourself, and gold and silver in your treasuries?
By your abundant knowledge and your trade you increased your strength; your heart was exalted in your strength.

triples.relationship: Tyre's accumulated gold and silver
triples.rationale: Zechariah describes Tyre storing immense silver and gold alongside fortifications. Ezekiel likewise describes gold and silver in Tyre's ruler's treasuries and increased strength through knowledge and trade. Both specifically portray that city's wealth and strength.
triples.source_text: Tyre built herself fortifications, stored silver like dust and gathered gold like the mud of the roads.

target_units.text: Surely it was not by your knowledge or understanding that you built up strength for yourself, and gold and silver in your treasuries?
By your abundant knowledge and your trade you increased your strength; your heart was exalted in your strength.

triples.relationship: Tyre's strength brought down into the sea
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces the Lord striking Tyre's strength into the sea. Ezekiel's Tyre oracle likewise describes strength brought down, possessions plundered and building materials thrown into the sea. The city, lowered strength and maritime destruction connect the judgments.
triples.source_text: Therefore the Lord will inherit her and strike her strength into the sea; she will be consumed by fire.

target_units.text: With his horses’ hoofs they will trample all your squares. He will kill your people with the sword and bring the support of your strength down to the ground.
He will plunder your strength, strip your possessions, throw down your walls, and demolish your desirable houses. He will throw your stones, timber, and dust into the sea.

triples.relationship: fire announced against Tyre
triples.rationale: Zechariah says Tyre will be consumed by fire after the Lord strikes her strength. Amos likewise announces fire upon Tyre's walls devouring her foundations. Both directly name the city and fiery destruction.
triples.source_text: Therefore the Lord will inherit her and strike her strength into the sea; she will be consumed by fire.

target_units.text: I will send fire upon Tyre’s walls, and it will devour her foundations.”

triples.relationship: judgment upon Gaza and Ashkelon
triples.rationale: Zechariah describes Gaza's suffering and loss of a king and Ashkelon's loss of habitation. Zephaniah likewise announces Gaza's plundering and Ashkelon's disappearance. The matching named cities connect the oracles while their particular outcomes remain distinct.
triples.source_text: Ashkelon will see and fear; Gaza will suffer greatly, and Akkaron too, because she was ashamed at her downfall. A king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will certainly not be inhabited.

target_units.text: For Gaza will be plundered and Ashkelon will disappear; Ashdod will be cast out at midday and Ekron uprooted.

triples.relationship: contrasting announcements concerning Azotus's inhabitants
triples.rationale: Zechariah says foreigners will dwell in Azotus while their arrogance is brought down. Amos announces destruction of inhabitants from Azotus. The shared city and its population provide the connection; the outcomes are not presented as identical.
triples.source_text: Foreigners will dwell in Azotus, and I will bring down the foreigners’ arrogance.

target_units.text: I will destroy inhabitants from Azotus, and a tribe will be removed from Ascalon. I will bring My hand against Accaron, and the remaining foreigners will perish,” says the Lord.

triples.relationship: historical context for the comparison with the Jebusite
triples.rationale: Zechariah compares Akkaron with the Jebusite within an announcement about remaining for God and belonging alongside Judah. Joshua records Jebusites continuing to live in Jerusalem when Judah could not destroy them. This supplies a concrete account of the named people remaining in Judah's setting, without identifying Akkaron with Jerusalem.
triples.source_text: I will remove their blood from their mouth and their detestable things from between their teeth. This one too will remain for our God; they will be like a commander of a thousand in Judah, and Akkaron like the Jebusite.

target_units.text: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the sons of Judah could not destroy them. The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem until that day.

triples.relationship: the protected holy city no longer traversed by outsiders
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises the Lord's stand for His house, preventing passage and renewed expulsion. Joel likewise names His dwelling in Zion and says foreigners will no longer pass through holy Jerusalem. Both connect divine presence with protection of that sacred place.
triples.source_text: I will take a stand for My house to prevent passing through or returning. No one driving them out will come upon them again, for now I have seen with My own eyes.

target_units.text: You will recognize that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion on My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy city, and foreigners will no longer pass through her.

triples.relationship: explicit later prophetic quotation applied to Jesus' entry
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces Zion's gentle king mounted on a beast of burden and young colt. Matthew explicitly introduces a fulfilled prophetic saying about Zion's meek king riding a donkey and colt, then narrates the disciples bringing them to Jesus. The named address, king and mounts establish the quotation relationship.
triples.source_text: Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion; proclaim, daughter Jerusalem. Behold, your king comes to you, righteous and saving, gentle, and mounted upon a beast of burden and a young colt.

target_units.text: This happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled:
“Tell the daughter of Zion: ‘Behold, your King comes to you, meek and mounted upon a donkey, and upon a colt, the foal of a beast of burden.’”
The disciples went and did as Jesus directed them.
They brought the donkey and the colt, placed the garments upon them, and He sat upon them.

triples.relationship: explicit written saying about Zion's king on a colt
triples.rationale: John introduces Jesus' sitting on a young donkey with a written saying addressing daughter Zion and announcing her king on a donkey's colt. Those elements correspond to Zechariah's announcement. John preserves its own introductory command not to fear rather than Zechariah's call to rejoice.
triples.source_text: Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion; proclaim, daughter Jerusalem. Behold, your king comes to you, righteous and saving, gentle, and mounted upon a beast of burden and a young colt.

target_units.text: Jesus found a young donkey and sat upon it, just as it is written,
“Do not fear, daughter Zion. Behold, your King comes, sitting upon a donkey’s colt.”
His disciples did not understand these things at first. But when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things were written about Him and that they had done these things to Him.

triples.relationship: royal peace and dominion extending to seas and rivers
triples.rationale: Zechariah's coming king is associated with destroyed battle weapons, abundant peace and rule reaching waters and river outlets. The royal psalm likewise combines abundant peace with rule from sea to sea and from the river to the world's ends. The expansive rule and peace connect them without making their geographical wording identical.
triples.source_text: He will destroy chariots from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem; the battle bow will be destroyed, and abundance and peace from the nations. He will rule waters as far as the sea and the earth’s river outlets.

target_units.text: Righteousness will arise in his days, and abundant peace until the moon is taken away.
And he will rule from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the inhabited world.

triples.relationship: explicit blood-of-the-covenant language
triples.rationale: Zechariah attributes the release of prisoners from a waterless pit to covenant blood. Exodus describes Moses sprinkling blood and identifying it as the blood of the covenant the Lord made with the people. The covenant-blood expression is shared, while prisoner release belongs to Zechariah's statement.
triples.source_text: You, by covenant blood, released your prisoners from a pit with no water.

target_units.text: Moses took half the blood and poured it into bowls; the other half he poured against the altar.
He took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people. They said, “We will do and obey everything the Lord has spoken.”
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it over the people, saying, “Behold, the blood of the covenant the Lord has made with you concerning all these words.”

triples.relationship: captivity pictured through a pit containing no water
triples.rationale: Zechariah speaks of prisoners released from a pit with no water. Genesis describes Joseph seized by his brothers and thrown into an empty pit expressly said to have no water. The particular waterless confinement image connects the passages, without identifying the prisoners as Joseph.
triples.source_text: You, by covenant blood, released your prisoners from a pit with no water.

target_units.text: And when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of the tunic of many colours which was upon him.
And they took him and cast him into the pit; and the pit was empty, having no water.

triples.relationship: Zion divinely equipped to overcome hostile nations
triples.rationale: Zechariah pictures Judah as the Lord's bent bow and Zion's children handled like a fighter's sword against Greek children. Micah likewise gives daughter Zion iron horns and bronze hooves to thresh hostile nations. Both turn God's people into an image of an empowered instrument against opponents, with different weapons and named enemies.
triples.source_text: For I bent you, Judah, as a bow for Myself; I filled Ephraim, and I will rouse your children, Zion, against the Greeks’ children and handle you like a fighter’s sword.

target_units.text: Now many nations have gathered against you, saying, “We will rejoice over her, and our eyes will look upon Zion!”
But they did not know the Lord’s thought or understand His counsel, for He gathered them like sheaves of a threshing floor.

Rise and thresh them, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horns iron and your hooves bronze. With them you will melt down nations and grind many peoples fine; you will dedicate their multitude to the Lord and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.

triples.relationship: the Lord's warfare pictured through missiles and lightning
triples.rationale: Zechariah describes the Lord above His people, a missile going like lightning and His threatening trumpet. The psalm likewise depicts His heavenly voice, arrows and lightning throwing enemies into turmoil. Both combine divine intervention with missile and lightning imagery, while the trumpet is particular to Zechariah here.
triples.source_text: The Lord will be over them; a missile will go out like lightning. The Lord Almighty will sound a trumpet and go in the tumult of His threat.

target_units.text: And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave His voice.
And He sent out arrows and scattered them; He multiplied lightning flashes and threw them into turmoil.

triples.relationship: the Lord explicitly shielding His people
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces that the Lord Almighty will shield the people in battle. Isaiah likewise says the Lord will shield Jerusalem, rescue, preserve and save. The stated protective action connects the promises without importing Zechariah's wine and altar images into Isaiah.
triples.source_text: The Lord Almighty will shield them. They will consume them, bury them with sling stones and drink them down like wine; they will fill the altar like bowls.

target_units.text: Like flying birds, so the Lord will shield Jerusalem, rescue, preserve and save.”

triples.relationship: the Lord saves and tends His people as sheep
triples.rationale: Zechariah says the Lord will save His people like sheep. Ezekiel likewise promises the Lord's personal search, gathering, feeding and care for His sheep. Both expressly describe divine preservation through the flock image.
triples.source_text: The Lord will save them on that day, His people like sheep, because holy stones roll over His land.

target_units.text: For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will seek out My sheep and visit them.

As a shepherd seeks his flock on a day when there is gloom and cloud among separated sheep, so I will seek out My sheep and drive them away from every place where they scattered on a day of cloud and gloom.

I will bring them out from the nations, gather them from the countries and bring them into their own land. I will feed them upon Israel’s mountains, in the ravines and in every dwelling place of the land.
I will feed them in good pasture, and their folds will be upon Israel’s high mountain. There they will lie down, there rest in good delight, and graze in rich pasture upon Israel’s mountains.
I Myself will feed My sheep and give them rest, and they will know that I am the Lord. Thus says the Lord, the Lord:
I will seek the lost, bring back the wandering, bind up the broken, strengthen the failing and guard the strong. I will feed them with judgment.

triples.relationship: grain and wine given with renewed favor toward the people
triples.rationale: Zechariah names grain for young men and fragrant wine for virgins within the account of the people's salvation. Joel likewise follows the Lord's sparing of His people with a promise of grain, wine and oil. Both connect renewed provision with restored divine favor.
triples.source_text: For whatever is good of him and whatever is beautiful from him: grain for young men and fragrant wine for virgins.

target_units.text: Then the Lord became jealous for His land and spared His people.
The Lord answered His people: “Look, I am sending out to you grain, wine and oil, and you will be filled with them. I will no longer give you over to reproach among the nations,
